learning_outcomes.text: Apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids, both isolated and integrated into complex structures.
Understand the characteristics and mechanical behavior of thermo-elastic, plastic, and composite solids and structures.

syllabus_topics: Hypotheses of Continuum Mechanics in solids.
Internal potential. Principle of Virtual Works.
Introduction to solution using the Finite Element Method (FEM).
Two-dimensional elasticity. Plane stress. Plane strain. Applications.
Formulas: Tension-compression, simple bending, skewed bending and compound bending.
Calculation of indeterminate beams. Force method.
Hypostatic beams. Thread theory. Application to cables and arches.
Supports and connections. Degree of indeterminacy.
Equilibrium. Solution of determinate structures. Displacements.
assessment_rules: The final grade is 0.65 times the Final Exam grade (NE) plus 0.35 times the Lab Practices grade (NP). A minimum score of 3.5 is required in the final exam; if not met, the final grade will be the minimum of 3.5 and the calculated grade. The final exam is recuperable, while lab practices are not, though their grade carries over. For global evaluation, both the final written exam (65%) and a practical exam (35%) are recuperable.
